checks.statement: Allow only one selected option in the group; use checkboxes when multiple selections are allowed.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from Usage: Allow only one selected option in the group; use checkboxes when multiple selections are allowed.

evidence.result: The cited specimen is a standalone web example; it contains no application screen/navigation policy that can enforce this condition: “When configuring a selection group.”.

implementation.notes: The condition is “When configuring a selection group.” and the instruction is “Allow only one selected option in the group; use checkboxes when multiple selections are allowed.”. This is an app-level content, layout, or product-selection decision; the standalone reusable control/specimen does not have the surrounding screen context needed to apply it. This disposition covers this exact condition only.

checks.statement: Arrow keys move focus and selection and wrap between first and last options; Space selects the focused option and does nothing if it is already selected.
checks.condition: When operating a radio group by keyboard.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from Keyboard navigation: Arrow keys move focus and selection and wrap between first and last options; Space selects the focused option

evidence.result: Each option is a native input type=radio with the same name within the group; the browser supplies radio-group arrow-key selection and wrapping semantics.

implementation.notes: Native same-name radio inputs provide one selected option and standard browser arrow/Space behavior. This is code-level evidence, not a browser exercise.

checks.statement: Clicking or tapping either the radio icon or its label selects it; apply selection immediately unless the containing dialog or page requires saving.
checks.condition: When a radio option is selected.

evidence.result: Each radio input and its custom icon and adjacent text are inside one wrapping `<label>`, so activating either the control or label selects the native radio input.

implementation.notes: The rendered label associates the visible option text and icon with the native radio; selection occurs through standard input behavior.

checks.statement: Do not apply density by default because targets can fall below 48×48 CSS pixels; if offering denser layouts, keep controls that change density at least 48×48 CSS pixels.

implementation.notes: The component uses its normal radio geometry and exposes no user density setting by default.

checks.statement: Use a 20dp radio icon, 40dp state layer and 48dp target.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from the captured Measurements prose or table: Use a 20dp radio icon, 40dp state layer and 48dp target.

evidence.result: The native input has a centered minimum 48x48 target while the icon and state-layer dimensions remain tokenized.
Chromium: the expanded radio input accepts hit tests in all four directions, activates once, and the visible root remains below 48px.

implementation.notes: Hit target exercised; exact 20px icon and 40px state-layer values remain code evidence rather than independently measured fixture assertions.

fixes.summary: Expand compact icon and radio hit targets to 48 pixels

checks.statement: People using assistive technology must be able to navigate to and select a radio option and receive feedback appropriate to their input.
checks.condition: When exposing radio groups to assistive technology.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated the explicit Use cases instruction: People using assistive technology must be able to navigate to and select a radio option and receive feedback a

evidence.result: The web specimen names the radiogroup through a legend and each option through a label; native radio inputs expose checked state. No screen-reader observation was performed.

implementation.notes: The DOM provides the expected web group/option names and native selection state, but announcement and feedback behavior has not been tested with assistive technology.

checks.statement: Selecting one radio deselects the others. Once selected, a group cannot be deselected; provide a No option/Not applicable option or a separate clear-selection action if opting out is needed.
checks.condition: When a radio group allows an initial selection.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from Interaction & style: Selecting one radio deselects the others. Once selected, a group cannot be deselected; provide a No option/Not

evidence.result: All options in a rendered group share the same radio `name`; one input is checked from the selected state, and native radio behavior does not toggle off the currently selected option.

implementation.notes: Same-name native radio inputs enforce single selection and preserve the selected option when activated again.

checks.statement: Tab enters the radio group on the selected option, or the first option if none is selected; Shift+Tab enters on the selected option, or the last option if none is selected. Arrow keys move focus and selection, wrapping between first and last options.
checks.condition: When focus enters a radio group.

evidence.result: The group is composed of same-name native radio inputs with one checked option or none; the browser implements radio-group Tab entry and arrow focus/selection behavior.

implementation.notes: Native radio keyboard semantics provide the selected/first Tab entry, selected/last Shift+Tab entry, and arrow traversal described by the source.

checks.statement: Use on-surface for adjacent label text and keep that text color unchanged between selected and unselected states.
checks.condition: When styling labels for radio buttons.

implementation.notes: The label text remains ordinary inherited text and is not switched between selected and unselected states by radio CSS.
